title: Mechanisms Underlying Asthma Exacerbations Prevented and Persistent With Immune-Based Therapy
brief_summary: Asthma is a growing problem, especially in children. It causes frequent wheezing, shortness of breath, chest tightness, and cough. A cold that is caused by a virus (viral cold) can sometimes make asthma symptoms worse. This study will help investigators learn about the way colds are related to asthma attacks among children who need higher amounts of medications to control their asthma. Investigators want to learn why viral colds sometimes cause asthma attacks and other times do not by studying the immune system response in samples taken from the nose and blood.
study_population: The MUPPITS study will enroll inner-city children 6-17 years of age with difficult-to-control, exacerbation-prone asthma. Approximately 150 children will be enrolled and followed prospectively.
